newsitem.title: JAPAN: Yen's weakness not justified by fundamentals--Card.
newsitem.headline: Yen's weakness not justified by fundamentals--Card.

text.p: The value of the yen remains weaker than the level which Japan's economic and financial fundamentals would justify, Andrew Card, president of the American Automobile Manufacturers Association, told reporters in Tokyo on Monday.
"The value of the yen still remains weaker than (the level which Japan's) economic and financial fundamentals would justify," Card said.
"I personally would like to see the dollar at about 100 yen," he said.
Earlier this month, the yen weakened to over 114 to the dollar, helped along by dollar-buying intervention by the Bank of Japan, he said.

It is one thing if economic fundamentals dictate a weak yen, but the reality is that the Bank of Japan deliberately pushed the yen lower over the past 18 months, far lower than the market alone would dictate, he said.

"I clearly feel the (yen) level over 110 is much, much too weak and when you get into the 115 range, you are in a danger zone. There is nothing that can support or justify a level that will be in a 114-115 range," Card said.
The yen was standing at 111.07 to the dollar at 0637 GMT.
